bull_bear.body:
- We do not have long-term agreements with a majority of our customers.
- We do not have firm, long-term supply agreements with most customers and primarily rely on purchase orders rather than fixed-term contracts.
- As a result, our customers may amend, reschedule, reduce, or cancel purchase orders prior to finalisation.
- Such changes could disrupt our production planning, lead to sub-optimal capacity utilisation, and adversely affect our revenues, margins, working capital and cash flows.
- Some customer purchase orders include provisions for remedies such as liquidated damages or specific performance in the event of delay or default.
- The loss of this significant or key customer or a reduction in the amount of business could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
- A reduction in these segments may result from factors such as changes in government procurement policies, budget allocations, adoption of new technologies, increased competition, or shifts in customer preferences.
- We are dependent on a limited number of suppliers for procurement of our raw materials, and the loss of any one or more of our major suppliers would have a material adverse effect on our business operations and profitability.

No combined objects total was produced. The RHP prints '[●]' for Total Net Proceeds and no total is fabricated here; total_net_proceeds_lakhs is null with an explanatory note.
project.total_cost_lakhs = 4442.00 is the RHP's own PRINTED 'Total Working Capital Gap (A-B)' for Projected Fiscal 2026-27, not a sum computed by this extraction.

Every 'crore' figure in the source Objects chapter is a SEBI regulatory threshold or ceiling, not an issuer money amount. The Rs. 10 Crores in the Objects-table footnote is the Regulation 230(2) GCP CEILING and has not been recorded as the GCP allocation.

Zeros recorded as real printed values: FY 2026-27 'Working Capital funding from Banks/Borrowings' = nil (dash), FY 2026-27 'Short Term Borrowings (excluding cc)' = nil (dash), FY 2025-26 'Short Term Borrowings (excluding cc)' = nil (dash).

Affirmative nil / not-applicable disclosures recorded in-field rather than by omitting the key: monitoring agency (not applicable), appraisal (none), bridge financing (none raised), green shoe (not applicable), IPO grading (not required), credit rating (not required), machinery/capex (no such object), capacity expansion (no such object).
No ratios were computed. The percentages carried in ratios_as_printed_pct are the RHP's own printed figures.

Roughly the final quarter of the Objects chapter was missing. The remainder was RECOVERED verbatim from the staged full text at D:\testvscode\streamlit-dashboard\src\utils\output\_scratch\rhp_kwick\KWICK_FULLTEXT.txt, section '===== SECTION: objects =====' (lines 8259-8455). Recovered content, none of which was present in the routed slice: (a) the tail of the FY24-25 vs FY25-26 variance table including Short Term Provisions and Total (B) 1,884.55 and Total Working Capital Gap 3,587.14; (b) the entire '3. GENERAL CORPORATE EXPENSES' section including the Rs. [●] Lakhs GCP amount and the Rs. 1,000 lakh cap wording; (c) the entire 'OFFER RELATED EXPENSES' section and the issue-expenses table (all '[●]') plus the per-application brokerage/processing fee structure; (d) 'Shortfall of Funds'; (e) 'Bridge Financing Facilities' (nil); (f) 'Monitoring of Utilization of Funds' (monitoring agency NOT APPLICABLE) - had this not been recovered, the monitoring-agency disclosure would have been wrongly recorded as absent; (g) 'Appraisal by Appraising Fund' (none of the Objects appraised); (h) 'Interim Use of Proceeds'; (i) 'Variation in Objects'; (j) 'Other Confirmations'. Cross-checks were additionally drawn from the same file's '===== SECTION: general_info =====' (MONITORING AGENCY / APPRAISING ENTITY / GREEN SHOE / IPO GRADING / CREDIT RATING, lines 5012-5026), '===== SECTION: the_offer =====' (offer composition, all amounts '[●]', lines 3678-3741) and '===== SECTION: risk_factors =====' (Risk Factor 11 working-capital figures, lines 1974-1981). A document-wide search for 'quotation', 'orders have been placed', 'purchase order' and 'proforma invoice' returned no machinery or capex procurement disclosure anywhere in the RHP, confirming the absence recorded in orders_not_placed is a true absence of the subject matter and not an extraction gap.

As the size of the Fresh Issue does not exceeds ₹ 5,000 Lakh, appointment of Monitoring Agency is not applicable to monitor the utilisation of the Net Proceeds in accordance with Regulation 262 of the SEBI ICDR Regulations prior to the filing of Red herring Prospectus with the ROC. internal_operational.risk: We do not have long-term agreements with a majority of our customers.
We do not have firm, long-term supply agreements with most customers and primarily rely on purchase orders rather than fixed-term contracts.
As a result, our customers may amend, reschedule, reduce, or cancel purchase orders prior to finalisation.

strategy_growth.risk: We derive majority of our revenue from Sales of Goods and Sales of Services and any reduction in the demand of such segment could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial conditions Our Company derives a substantial portion of its revenue from Sales of Goods- comprising Forensic Science & Physical Evidence Solutions, Mobile CSI Vehicles, Cyber & Digital Forensics, and DNA Forensics—and Sales of Services, which primarily include renting of forensic equipment and AMC & other related services.
Further, our product span across Forensic Science & Physical Evidence Solutions, Mobile CSI Vehicles, Cyber & Digital Forensics, DNA Forensics.

The contribution of the Cyber segment, which operates at relatively lower gross margins and consequently entails higher procurement costs, increased from 23.18% in the previous year to 33.32% in the current year, resulting in a corresponding increase in purchase costs.
